 Judgment

Though these appeals are listed for admission, they are taken up for final disposal with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.
2.

These two appeals are directed against the judgment and award dated 15.09.2016 passed in MVC No.1565/2014 on the file of the learned VI Addl. Dist. & Sessions Judge & Addl. M.A.C.T., Belagavi (for short, 'Tribunal').

sentences.text:
3. The claimants are in appeal praying for enhancement of compensation but learned counsel Sri.Vitthal S.Teli for the claimants at the time of hearing would submit that the appellants-claimants would restrict their appeal for release of the compensation amount instead of keeping it in fixed deposit as ordered by the Tribunal; whereas the Insurance Company is in appeal questioning the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
4.

Brief facts of the case are that, the appellants-claimants, who are the wife, son and mother of the deceased Shivaji Kalal, filed a claim petition under Section 166 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7836-DB of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of Shivaji Kalal in a road traffic accident that took place on 07.07.2014 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-49-K-0459.

It is stated that the deceased was a Conductor in NWKRTC, he was receiving salary from NWKRTC and was aged 41 years as on the date of the accident.
5.
On issuance of notice, respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their written statement admitting the insurance policy but denied all other averments made in the claim petition.
It further contended that the deceased was working in NWKRTC, but was suspended from service and he was not keeping good health as on the date of the accident.

6. Before the Tribunal, claimant No.1-wife of the deceased examined herself as PW1 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P11; whereas the respondent No.2 examined RW1 and marked documents as Exs.R1 to R3.

The Tribunal based on the material on record allowed the claim petition in part and awarded a total compensation of Rs.41,73,667/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization and while awarding NC: 2024:KHC-D:7836-DB compensation

, the Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.28,960/- per month,
deducted 10% towards income tax, added 30% of the assessed income towards future prospects,
adopted multiplier of 14 and deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased.

7. Heard the learned counsel Sri.Vittal S.Teli for the appellants-claimants, learned counsel Sri.Ravindra R.Mane appearing for Insurance Company and perused the appeal papers along with original records.
8.
Sri.Vittal S.Teli, learned counsel appearing for appellants-claimants would contend that the income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.28,690/- per month is proper and correct.

Learned counsel would submit that the deceased was working as Conductor in NWKRTC who was dismissed from Smt.Laxmi W/O. Shivaji Kalal vs Mr.Raju S/O. Yallappa Kalal on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93129701/
4 service on 25.08.2011 which was the subject matter of the proceedings before the Addl. Labour Court, Hubli in KID No.143/2011.

entities.text: Smt.Laxmi W/O. Shivaji Kalal vs Mr.Raju S/O. Yallappa Kalal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said KID petition was allowed on 29.03.2012 directing the respondent-NWKRTC to reinstate the deceased into service with full back wages and other consequential benefits from the date of dismissal till the date of reinstatement.

Therefore, he NC:
2024:KHC-D:7836-DB submits that the income of the deceased ought to be determined as if he was working as a conductor in NWKRTC.
Learned counsel would submit that the appeal of the claimants is restricted only to release of entire compensation amount.

9. Learned counsel Sri.Ravindra R.Mane appearing for the Insurance Company would vehemently contend that there is no material whatsoever to establish the income of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
It is further submitted that the deceased was dismissed from service on 25.08.2011.
Though the Labour Court award directs reinstatement on 29.03.2012, till his death the deceased was not reinstated and the deceased was not receiving salary from NWKRTC.
Thus, he submits that the Tribunal committed grave error in assessing the income of the deceased based on his earlier salary certificate.

Further, learned counsel would also submit that as per Exs.P10 and P11, the salary of the deceased is stated at Rs.16,950/- per month, but as against Exs.P10 and P11, the Tribunal has committed grave error in taking Rs.16,000/- as basic and adding 71% DA and 10% HRA.

Learned counsel referring to Exs.P10 and P11 would submit that the salary of the deceased was Rs.16,950/-
per month and the Tribunal NC: 2024:KHC-D:7836-DB could not have taken Rs.16,000/- as basic and added 71% as DA and 10% as HRA to arrive at Rs.28,960/- per month as income of the deceased.
Thus, learned counsel submits that the claimants would be entitled for compensation only based on notional income.

Learned counsel further submits that the rate of interest at 9% p.a.
awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and hence, prays for reducing it to 6% p.a., which would be just and appropriate.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the only point which falls for our consideration is as to whether the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal requires interference?

The above point is answered in the affirmative for the following reasons:
11.

The accident that took place on 07.07.2014 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-49/K-0459, resultant death of Shivaji Kalal, husband of claimant No.1 is not NC:
2024:KHC-D:7836-DB in dispute in this appeal.
There is no dispute with regard to the fact that the deceased was working as Conductor in the NWKRTC and his dismissal from service on 25.08.2011.

It is also not in dispute that in terms of Ex.P8-Award dated 29.03.2012 in KID No.143/2011 passed by the Additional Labour Court, Hubli, the order of dismissal of the deceased by the NWKRTC was set aside and the NWKRTC was directed to reinstate the deceased by paying full back wages and other consequent benefits.
12.

When once the order of dismissal is set aside and when the Labour Court directs reinstatement into service, it is clear that the deceased deemed to have continued in service as Conductor in the peculiar facts of the case for determing compensation on the head of dependency.

Moreover, it is to Smt.Laxmi W/O. Shivaji Kalal vs Mr.Raju S/O. Yallappa Kalal on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93129701/
5 be noted that the NWKRTC challenged the award of the Labour Court in Writ Petition No.106605/2016 before this Court.

sentences.text: This Court by order dated 12.03.2018 disposed off the writ petition as abated in view of the death of the deceased Sri.Shivaji Kalal.

13. The Tribunal erroneously assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.28,960/- per month taking note of basic - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7836-DB salary of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month and added 71% of DA and 10% of HRA to Rs.16,000/- to arrive at Rs.28,960/- per month which is wholly erroneous.
The claimants have placed on record Exs.P10 and P11.
Ex. P11-
Endorsement
issued to Ex.P10-Application under Right to Information Act
reveals that the deceased was receiving a salary of Rs.16,950/- per month.
Ex. P11
would not indicate other details of salary of the deceased.

Therefore, in the absence of any particulars or details or corroborative material, it would be appropriate to take Rs.16,950/- per month as salary of the deceased including DA, HRA and all other allowances.
To add 71% DA and 10% HRA there is no material

, therefore, we assess the income of the deceased at Rs.16,950/- per month based on Ex.P11.
14.
The deceased was aged 41 years as on the date of the accident and the Tribunal has rightly added 30% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
Taking note of the dependants at 3, 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, which is proper and correct.
Taking note of the age of the deceased at 41 years, multiplier of 14 is taken, which is also proper and correct.

Thus, the claimants would be - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7836-DB entitled for a modified compensation on the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.16,950 + 30%(future prospects) X 12(months) x 14(multiplier) x 2/3(deduction) =
Rs.24,67,920/-
15.
The claimants would be entitled for consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each apart from Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

The Tribunal has erred in awarding a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- on the head of loss of estate and Rs.50,000/- on the head of loss of love and affection towards mother which is contrary to decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others1.
16.

2. Loss of estate & Funeral 30,000/-

Learned counsel Sri.Ravindra R.Mane for Insurance Company further submitted that the interest granted at the rate of 9% per annum on the compensation amount would be on the higher side and taking note of the bank rates, he submits that award of 6% interest would be appropriate.
18. The submission of the learned counsel on rate of interest deserves to be considered.

Taking note of today's rate of bank interest, we deem it appropriate to reduce rate of interest from 9% p.a. to 6%
p.a.
19.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.26,17,920/- as against Rs.41,73,667/- awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of claim petition till realization of the award amount.

20. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7836-DB b) The impugned judgment & award of Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.26,17,920/- as against Rs.41,73,667/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The entire compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization.
d) Insurance Company shall deposit  compensation amount with accrued Smt.Laxmi W/O. Shivaji Kalal vs Mr.Raju S/O. Yallappa Kalal on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93129701/
7 interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
